Plot Sample or Exposure Clusters

Source: R/plot_clusters.R
plot_clusters.Rd

Generates a heatmap of either sample clustering or exposure clustering results, split by cluster group.

Usage

plot_clusters(
  exposomicset,
  cluster_type = c("sample", "exposure"),
  exposure_cols = NULL
)

Arguments

exposomicset

A MultiAssayExperiment object containing clustering results in metadata(exposomicset)$quality_control.

cluster_type

A character string specifying which clustering to plot: "sample" (from run_cluster_samples()) or "exposure" (from run_cluster_exposures()). Default is "sample".

exposure_cols

A character vector specifying columns from colData to include in the heatmap. Default is NULL, which includes all colData columns for "sample" and all clustered exposures for "exposure".

Value

A ComplexHeatmap plot displaying clustering results.

Details

This function:

  • Extracts cluster assignments from metadata(exposomicset)$quality_control.

  • Merges cluster labels with colData(exposomicset) and the codebook.

  • Plots a heatmap split by sample groups (columns) or exposure groups (rows), with annotation tiles for exposure category and cluster group.

Examples

# create example data
mae <- make_example_data(
    n_samples = 30,
    return_mae = TRUE
)
#> Ensuring all omics datasets are matrices with column names.
#> Creating SummarizedExperiment objects.
#> Creating MultiAssayExperiment object.
#> MultiAssayExperiment created successfully.

exposure_cols <- c("exposure_pm25", "exposure_no2", "age", "bmi")

# determine sample and exposure clusters
mae <- mae |>
    run_cluster_samples(
        exposure_cols = exposure_cols,
        clustering_approach = "diana"
    ) |>
    run_cluster_exposures(
        exposure_cols = exposure_cols,
        clustering_approach = "diana"
    )
#> Starting exposure clustering analysis...
#> Starting clustering analysis...
#> Optimal number of clusters for samples: 22
#> Optimal number of clusters for exposures: 1

# plot sample clusters
sample_cluster_p <- mae |>
    plot_clusters(
        cluster_type = "sample",
        exposure_cols = exposure_cols
    )
#> tidyHeatmap says: If you use tidyHeatmap for scientific research, please cite: Mangiola, S. and Papenfuss, A.T., 2020. 'tidyHeatmap: an R package for modular heatmap production based on tidy principles.' Journal of Open Source Software. doi:10.21105/joss.02472.
